summary: Preserve conditional idle repository polling with inclusive timestamp boundaries, resumable overlap pagination and bounded admission endpoint/status attribution.

replay.detail: No graph replay or stored-state backfill. Older observer cursors default optional overlap maps and continuation URLs and safely replay their first overlap.

schema.detail: Storage version unchanged. No database migration. Optional cursor fields preserve old records. The strict local reservation ledger retains exactly its original at/caller/resource/observer/count shape; bounded endpoint/response attribution is stored in a separate diagnostic sidecar.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or coordinated upgrade requirement. Shared-token admission remains local to each daemon.

compatibility.detail: Repository item and comment requests overlap the stored watermark by one second and deduplicate by identity, update time and content digest, including repeated edits within the same second. Paginated sweeps preserve exact continuations, freeze the starting watermark and revalidate complete ordered page versions until two sweeps agree before advancing it. After two nonmatching completed sweeps, continuation falls back to ordinary observer cadence while retaining scan state and frozen watermarks; an unstable sweep is never force-committed. Idle URLs remain stable for ETag revalidation. Doctor adds bounded endpoint/status counts from a separate diagnostic sidecar, distinguishing 304 hits from possible quota-bearing requests; 304s still consume conservative local admission reservations. Admission safety depends only on the original ledger; attribution read/write failures expose a gap without blocking HTTP. This change does not alter watch cadence or stopped-seat watch lifecycle.

downtime.detail: No additional downtime or special rollout sequence. No live daemon is changed by this source patch.

manual.detail: No configuration change, migration or backfill required. Fleet owner election and rate-limit-header backoff remain design-only options in docs/st3/github-observer-admission.md.

recovery.detail: Rollback requires no storage migration or reservation deletion. Older readers ignore optional cursor fields and never read the attribution sidecar. Reservation bytes retain exactly the old strict schema, so older enforced-cap binaries preserve spent usage and continue admitting safely. Requests without sidecar records are unknown attribution after upgrading again.
